summary: Kickoff call to align on Lumen Therapy onboarding for Redwood inference. Covered integration points, expected throughput, security requirements, and pilot timeline. Agreed to run 2-week pilot on dedicated capacity with options for private VPC if needed.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Oliver Park (CTO, Lumen), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Security), Eve Dawson (PM)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): hey everyone thanks for joining, can you all hear me okay? we can see a few people joining in the background, welcome to the Redwood onboarding kickoff for Lumen Therapy. quick agenda: overview, integrations, security, pilot plan, next steps.
00:22 Speaker 2 (Oliver Park): yeah all good on our end, thanks Maya. excited to get this started.
00:30 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): perfect. quick intros, diego is our solutions engineer, he'll lead the technical deep dive, priya is your success manager. diego you want to add?
00:39 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): yep hi everyone, i'll cover infra, vpc options, and what we need for a pilot. quick note we typically start customers on dedicated capacity for predictable latency but we can also do hosted or private vpc depending on requirements.
00:58 Speaker 4 (Maya Singh): great thanks. high level from our side — we're rolling LLM features into our patient triage flow. initial scope is classification + short text generation for triage instructions. latency is sensitive during peak hours, target p95 under 600ms, throughput around 200 qps for short payloads.
01:18 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): ok that's helpful. 200 qps is in range for our dedicated pools, depending on model choice and batching. can you confirm average sequence length? prompts or user messages typically 50 tokens?
01:31 Speaker 4 (Maya Singh): yeah average is ~60 tokens, sometimes up to 200 for longer notes.
01:39 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): got it. that influences kernel selection and batching. for 60 tokens we can optimize for that profile; we also have quantization recommendations if you want to reduce cost.
01:51 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): quick security question — we are highly regulated, need SOC 2, audit logs, and data residency. what's Redwood's posture on KMS and SSO?
02:04 Speaker 2 (Maya Chen): good question. priya will share SOC2 and compliance docs after this call. we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and have SAML SSO + RBAC for the console. for hosted API we have encryption at rest and audit logs retained per plan.
02:20 Speaker 5 (Priya Rao): just to add, we can provide a security addendum and we also offer longer log retention as an add-on. we'll include specifics in the follow-up.
02:32 Speaker 4 (Eve Dawson): can you explain the difference between dedicated and private? Oliver is concerned about data exfil and isolation.
02:41 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): sure — dedicated means reserved GPU pools in our infra with tenant isolation and SLA-backed capacity. private (VPC/on-prem) means the control plane can be in our cloud but the runtime can sit inside your VPC or even on-prem; you control networking and KMS. dedicated is faster to start, private adds stronger network-level isolation. there are tradeoffs on onboarding time and cost.
03:08 Speaker 2 (Maya Chen): and we offer autoscaling for dedicated pools with burst capacity, so you get predictable baseline and can handle spikes.
03:16 Speaker 4 (Maya Singh): in terms of model, we're leaning towards an open model to avoid export constraints, but quality matters. do you have model recommendations?
03:27 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): yes — for short generation tasks we'll recommend a mid-sized, quantized model we verified — it balances throughput and latency. we can also run a small benchmark during pilot to validate p95 latency and token costs.
03:42 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): pilot is usually 2 weeks: integration, run load tests, validate latency/cost/quality. recommended success criteria: p95 < 600ms, less than X cost per 1k queries (we'll estimate), and no major accuracy regressions on seed prompts.
04:00 Speaker 6 (Eve Dawson): what's X cost per 1k? we need a ballpark to budget.
04:06 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): depends on model and batching; we'll send a baseline price estimate in the follow-up. for dedicated it's usage plus reserved capacity commit. we can model costs with your expected qps and sequence length.
04:18 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): about logs — can you stream audit logs to our SIEM? we prefer syslog/CloudWatch or S3 delivery.
04:29 Speaker 2 (Maya Chen): yes we support log exports to S3 and integrations to common SIEMs. for private VPC we can also push logs to your endpoints.
04:41 Speaker 4 (Oliver Park): timeline — we are hoping to run pilot within two weeks. is that reasonable?
04:48 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): if we focus on dedicated pilot it's realistic: day 1 integration (API keys, sample calls), day 2-3 load testing and benchmarking, remainder for tweaks and quality checks. for private VPC onboarding add a week for network setup.
05:02 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): ok sounds like a plan. next steps we'll send the onboarding checklist and security docs. diego will schedule a deeper technical call to discuss VPC CIDR, peering, and KMS.
05:13 Speaker 6 (Eve Dawson): who will be our main point of contact for escalations?
05:18 Speaker 2 (Maya Chen): priya is your CSM for day-to-day, diego for technical, and I will own commercial questions. we'll include support SLAs in the doc.
05:28 Speaker 4 (Maya Singh): one more thing — can we run a short quality eval on our seed prompts before pilot? want to make sure generation fidelity is acceptable.
05:36 Speaker 3 (Diego Alvarez): absolutely, send a set of 50 prompts and we will run them during the initial test and report back on quality drift and recommendations.
05:46 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): regarding compliance, we might need a security review with our legal and infosec. can we schedule that?
05:53 Speaker 2 (Maya Chen): yes we do security_review calls regularly; priya will propose times. we'll bring our security engineer for that meeting.
06:02 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): quick recap and owners: Maya to send onboarding checklist and pricing, priya to send SOC2 and compliance pack, diego to set up deep dive on VPC and run initial benchmark, Oliver to share network diagram and throughput targets, Maya S to share 50 seed prompts.
06:20 Speaker 4 (Oliver Park): sounds good, we'll aim to get diagrams and prompts over this week.
06:26 Speaker 6 (Eve Dawson): thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
06:29 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): great thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and calendar invites. bye!

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "diego" spelled correctly mostly but product names sometimes fuzzy), some timestamps are approximate. The call included typical negotiation around cost/latency tradeoffs, and clear ask for SOC2 and network diagram.

Attachments mentioned: onboarding_checklist.xlsx (to be shared), SOC2_report.pdf (to be shared), sample_prompts.csv (customer), network_diagram.png (customer).
